In all these matters, the applicants have prayed that the First Information Reports registered for the offence 179, 188, 328 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) read with Section 59 (iii) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (in short "the Act of 2006") be quashed.

The main thrust of challenge is that the allegation in the FIR does not spell out offence under the provisions of the Act of 2006 and Rules framed under it and consequently offence under section of the IPC is not made out.
2.

This Court on 02.08.2014 issued notices to the non- applicants and by way of ad-interim order it was directed that the investigation may proceed but, charge-sheets under Section 328 of the IPC may not be filed.
By order dated 31.10.2014, the present application along with connected matters was admitted and interim order granted earlier was confirmed.

Shri R. L. Khapre, learned Senior Advocate a/w. Shri S. A. Mohta, Advocate for the applicants submitted that the Division Bench of this Court at Aurangabad in Criminal Writ Petition No.
1027/2015 has adjudicated similar issue in group of the matters along with Writ Petition No.
1027/2015.

opennyai_summary.facts:
In all these matters, the applicants have prayed that the First Information Reports registered for the offence 179, 188, 328 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) read with Section 59 (iii) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (in short "the Act of 2006") be quashed.
The non-applicant no. 1 has filed reply and submitted that registration of the FIR under Section 328 of the IPC cannot be faulted, as the material on record fulfills ingredients of Section 328 of the IPC.
[2018 AIR (SC) 5348] and submitted that it is open for the Food Safety Officer to independently filed complaint before the Competent Court for the offence under provision of the Act of 2006.
opennyai_summary.arguments: It is also submitted by Shri R. L. Khapre, learned Senior Advocate that from the averments in the FIR, ingredients of the offence alleged against the applicants are not fulfilled.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
He also invited attention of this Court to the order passed by the Division Bench of this Court in LD-VC-CRI-APPLICATION (APPA) No. 452/2020 in the case of Ritesh Rajkumar Toshniwal Vs.
State of 27 cr-apl-444-14j+45.odt Maharashtra (one of us Justice Z. A. Haq is a party) and submitted that similar order be passed in the present applications as facts of these batch of applications are similar.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In the present matters also, the investigation is completed and charge-sheets are ready.
In our view, interest of justice would sub- served by passing following order :-
(i) The Investigating Agency shall file charge-sheets within one month from today.
(ii) The Food Safety Officer will be at liberty to file complaint under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
(iii) As we have not delved into the issues raised by the applicants, it will be open to the applicants to avail appropriate remedy for redressal of their grievances, as per law, after filing of the charge- sheets.
All criminal applications are disposed in the above terms.
